messages:
satoshi: FYI observed a recurring "stall wave" on the kv-pool hosts during high-refill windows. alloc latency spikes cluster ~500-800ms apart and line up with cuMemAlloc fallbacks. attaching a short nsys slice (18s) and a tiny perfetto snippet.

maya: can you drop the trace here? is this during a cold fill from disk or just long-tail tail evictions? :eyes:

satoshi: uploading nsys -> https://artifacts/internal/nsys/1812345678-slice.qdtrace (private). it's during a KV cache miss burst when many requests miss the prefix cache and trigger new weights/kv state materialization. not disk IO, it's allocator pressure.

satoshi: nsys command used:
```
nsys profile --output=1812345678-slice --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-annotation-mode=sync --duration=18
```

satoshi: quick extracted timeline from the trace (trimmed):
```
[00:00:02.112] host: enqueue request -> prefetch-kv (0.6ms)
[00:00:02.118] kernel: kv_materialize (1.8ms)
[00:00:02.120] host: cuMemAlloc fallback (blocking) (54ms)
[00:00:02.176] kernel: small-gemm (0.9ms)
[00:00:02.760] host: cuMemAlloc fallback (blocking) (48ms)
[00:00:03.308] host: cuMemAlloc fallback (blocking) (63ms)
```

jun: interesting — those 40-60ms host allocs are consistent with falling back out of our arena/pool. can you paste allocator counters? pool hits vs misses?

satoshi: counters from the run (debug dump):
```
pool_total_allocs: 12837
pool_hit: 12004
pool_miss: 833
pool_evictions: 42
avg_slab_size: 1.1MB
free_chunks: 9
```

liam: free_chunks=9 + avg_slab 1.1MB suggests fragmentation. if many threads need ~3-4MB at once we fragment and driver allocs happen. what are our min_slab and max_slab thresholds on that host?

satoshi: min_slab=512KB, max_slab=8MB, slab_split_threshold=1.0 (prod).

jun: hypothesis: when several small requests free memory in patterns that leave many <1MB holes, the pool won't satisfy 3-4MB requests so they go to cuMemAlloc. also our slab_split_threshold at 1.0 prevents smart coalescing. propose: test increasing min_slab to 1MB and enabling eager-coalesce for second slice.

maya: also worth checking hostalloc vs device allocations — I saw NVTX that hostalloc is being used in some tokenization code path which pins pages and slows down the allocator. liam, can you confirm if tokenization uses HostAllocator now?

liam: tokenization uses host pinned pages for the CPU->GPU transfer path (to avoid staging copies). that can increase page lock pressure. but the trace shows the slowdown at the point of cuMemAlloc, so I think fragmentation is primary.

perf-bot: [alert] alloc-latency-anomaly detected on kvpool-rank-2 at 2026-07-12T10:24:38Z: 95th pct host cuMemAlloc latency=68ms (baseline 5ms). Sample size=1200 requests.

satoshi: ran a repro with REDWOOD_ALLOC_TRACE=1 and REDWOOD_POOL_DEBUG=1. attached JSON counters: https://artifacts/internal/alloc/1812345678-counters.json

satoshi: short sample of the debug log showing fallback path:
```
[alloc] requested=3.5MB -> try_slab_bucket(4MB) -> candidate_slab_found=false -> fallback_to_driver cuMemAlloc -> blocking
[pool] free_list: 7 chunks < 4MB, total_free=7.9MB
```

jun: proposal for experiment: increment min_slab to 1MB, set slab_split_threshold=0.5, enable eager_coalesce=true, then run a 1-hour canary against heavy-kv-refill test and measure 95/99 pct allocation latency and pool_miss delta. rollback if CPU page pressure increases.

maya: agree. also instrument a perfetto full-trace to capture host-side stack traces around cuMemAlloc to ensure we don't miss an unexpected path. use small 120s capture with filters: cudaDriverApi, host_alloc, kernel.

satoshi: I'll schedule the canary on a spare shard tomorrow and post results. quick note: we should also add a micro-benchmark that simulates concurrent 3-4MB allocations to measure fragmentation sensitivity.

liam: ack. I'll audit tokenization hostalloc usage to see if we can batch staging into fewer bigger pinned buffers (reduce lock churn).

maya: thanks — if the canary reduces pool_miss by >80% and median alloc latency drops under 8ms we can roll to prod with a staged 10% rollout. :thumbsup:

satoshi: cool. saving the nsys slice and perfetto link in the incident artifacts. I'll paste follow-up results in this thread. :white_check_mark:
